title: The Gap Is Load-Bearing
subtitle: Baby Baby, and the database constraint nobody should have to read aloud
description: A short, deliberately loose conversation about the Baby Baby app: a three-tap design constraint, a dial with a gap you cannot drag past, and the fourth allowed value in an enum.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Okay, this week I want to talk about Baby Baby. Which is, and I want to be really clear about this, the actual name of the repository.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: [laughs] You named it twice.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: I named it twice.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Was Baby taken?

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: [amused] Probably. Look, it tracks feeding, sleep and diapers. One URL, one database. Whoever logs something, everyone sees it.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: The design constraint is the good part though. Read me the constraint.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Logging something should take two or three taps. One handed. In the dark. While holding a baby.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Most honest performance requirement I've ever heard. Can you do it one handed at three in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: And everything falls out of that. There are no date pickers anywhere in the app.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: None?

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Zero. Everything defaults to right now. You tap it to nudge it, five minutes at a time.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Because nobody is opening a calendar at three in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: You're already on today. [dryly] You've been on today for nineteen hours.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: [laughs] Okay, that's bleak.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: The feed dial is my favourite piece of engineering pettiness. Two hundred and seventy degree drag dial, nought to two hundred millilitres—

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Why two seventy? Why not go all the way round?

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Because a full circle wraps. You drag past two hundred and land on zero. The gap exists so your thumb physically can't do that.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: So the gap is load-bearing.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: The gap is load-bearing. And it opens on whatever the last feed was, because the best predictor of the next feed is the last feed.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: [dryly] Deep learning.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: State of the art.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Alright, tell me about the sleep thing. You got weirdly animated about this on the phone.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: The baby being asleep is just a row with an empty end time. And that has to be true on every phone in the house at once. So Postgres enforces it, not the interface. One open session. Ever.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: And if two people put her down at the same time?

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Second one gets a rejection back carrying the session that's already running, and their app just quietly adopts it.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: So you built conflict resolution for two parents doing the same job without telling each other.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: [laughs] Yeah. That's marriage. It's in the schema.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: What are you proudest of that nobody would ever notice?

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Weights aren't events.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Go on.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Everything else answers what happened, and when. A weight answers what she is. That doesn't stop being true because it fell outside the window you're looking at.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: [amused] Bit philosophical for a nappy app.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: It's a family nappy app. We contain multitudes.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Speaking of. Diaper types.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: [sighs] I knew you were going to go there.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Four allowed values. Pee. Poop. Both. And read me the fourth one.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Massive blowout.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: [laughs] In the database. As a constraint.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: There is a check constraint in a production Postgres instance with the words massive blowout in it, and it will outlive both of us.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: That's her permanent record. That's forever.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: She'll thank me.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: [dryly] She will not thank you.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: [laughs] She will not thank me. That's Baby Baby.

chapters.title: One sleep to rule them all
